extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, and practitioners who submit comments on SSA information collections (including OMB Desk Officers, state/local governments, SSA beneficiaries, and professionals)
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register notice soliciting public comments on multiple Social Security Administration information collections submitted for OMB clearance under the Paperwork Reduction Act, including instructions on what issues to comment on, submission methods, and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics solicited for public comment
rubrics_metrics.description: SSA is soliciting comments on the accuracy of the agency's burden estimate; the need for the information; its practical utility; ways to enhance its quality, utility, and clarity; and ways to minimize burden on respondents, including the use of automated collection techniques or other forms of information technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments by the stated deadline to OMB Desk Officer and SSA Reports Clearance Officer or via reginfo.gov; reference Docket ID Number [SSA-2025-0005] in responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of comments (deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered SSA must receive comments no later than May 12, 2025 for the I. pending collection; for collections submitted to OMB in section II, comments should be received 30 days from the date of publication (no later than April 10, 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submissions arrive by specified dates; different collections in the notice have different comment deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirements and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments may be mailed, emailed, faxed, or submitted via reginfo.gov and must reference Docket ID Number SSA-2025-0005.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses and fax numbers provided in the notice; online submissions should use https://www.reginfo.gov/ and choose SSA's published item under Currently under Review—Open for Public Comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden estimate reporting components
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate components must include modality of completion, number of respondents, frequency of response, average burden per response (minutes), estimated total annual burden (hours), average theoretical hourly cost amount, and total annual opportunity cost (dollars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SSA provides detailed tables using these components for each information collection; commenters should address the accuracy of these components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of cost figures
rubrics_metrics.description: The average theoretical hourly cost and total annual opportunity cost figures presented are theoretical opportunity costs for respondents' time and do not represent actual charges imposed on respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should note that these are estimates based on BLS wage data and SSA management information and may comment on their appropriateness or calculation method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode preference and contingency for paper forms
rubrics_metrics.description: SSA prefers electronic or interview modalities (MCS/iClaim); paper forms are used only when SSA cannot conduct a personal interview or the respondent cannot use the internet claim system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing modality burdens, consider SSA's stated preference and the situations where paper remains necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy review methodology for SSI Quality Review Case Analysis (SSA-8508-BK / e8508)
rubrics_metrics.description: SSA selects a stratified random sample of recipients monthly, reviewers examine case files, prepare an initial contact letter with a checklist, conduct phone-based interviews to redevelop and verify non-medical eligibility factors and payment amount, document responses on the electronic SSA-8508-BK (or paper SSA-8508-BK if system inaccessible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters can address sample design, documentation requests, interview procedures, data collection tools (e8508), and respondent burden associated with this methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial documentation requirement for overpayment waiver/change (SSA-632-BK; SSA-634)
rubrics_metrics.description: When requesting a waiver of overpayment recovery or a change in overpayment recovery rate, respondents must provide financial information to help SSA determine how much the overpaid person can afford to repay each month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments may address the adequacy, intrusiveness, or alternatives to the financial information requested and ways to reduce respondent burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information elements for Request for Hearing by Administrative Law Judge (HA-501 / MCS / i501)
rubrics_metrics.description: SSA uses submitted information to determine if the hearing request was filed timely, whether the requester is the proper party, whether steps to obtain the right to a hearing were taken, the individual's reasons for disagreement, additional evidence to submit, hearing format preference (oral or record), and whether the individual has or wants a representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters can evaluate whether the form captures all necessary elements, whether questions are clear, and whether collection methods minimize respondent effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage reporting for State and Local Government employees (20 CFR 404 collections)
rubrics_metrics.description: States and interstate instrumentalities must provide wage and deposit contribution information for pre-1987 periods; SSA uses these regulations until pending items with states are closed out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments may address the continuing need for these collections, potential systems to improve accuracy, and burden estimates (note SSA used placeholder respondent counts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer satisfaction surveys standards under E.O. 12862
rubrics_metrics.description: Surveys are voluntary and assess customer satisfaction with the timeliness, appropriateness, access, and overall quality of SSA services and proposed modifications or new services; modalities include paper, internet, telephone, mailed questionnaires, and comment cards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters may suggest improvements in survey design, question clarity, sampling, and methods to reduce respondent burden while maintaining utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and data use for Social Security Benefits Applications (SSA-1, SSA-2, SSA-16, MCS, iClaim)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information collections determine applicants' eligibility for retirement, survivors, and disability benefits and the amount of benefits; disability applicants may file concurrent applications under Title II and Title XVI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments can address which data elements are necessary for eligibility determinations across modalities, redundancy across forms, and opportunities to streamline or clarify questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction and accuracy of published burden information
rubrics_metrics.description: When errors are found in previously published burden information (as noted for a prior notice on January 15, 2025), SSA issues corrections to the charts and tables showing burden estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters may point out inaccuracies and provide corrected data or methodology recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration request information requirements (SSA-561 / MCS / i561)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections document requests for reconsideration of initial determinations and are used to determine an individual's eligibility or entitlement to various SSA benefits; modalities include paper form, MCS/SSI Claims System, and internet iAppeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments may evaluate clarity, necessary data elements, and burden across modalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sampling and reviewer procedures as a burden/quality tradeoff
rubrics_metrics.description: SSA describes using stratified random sampling, pre-interview file reviews, checklists in initial letters, and phone-based interviews that may request mailed documentation—procedural choices that affect both data quality and respondent burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should consider whether the sampling and review procedures are appropriately designed to meet quality goals while minimizing respondent burden and may suggest automation or alternative designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference and reliance on external data sources for cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: SSA bases theoretical hourly cost figures on average U.S. worker wages from BLS and uses SSA management data for wait times and other inputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments may critique choice of wage data, wait time assumptions, or suggest better sources/methods for estimating opportunity costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction to obtain copies of collection instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals can obtain copies of the collection instruments by writing to OR.Reports.Clearance@ssa.gov (or using provided addresses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters seeking to review or test instruments should request copies in time to submit informed comments by the deadline.
